To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angular distribution of the Li ^{+} ions shows characteristic maxima of the scattering intensity at scattering angles of the order of 0.001 rad.
the interaction between a Li ^{+7} -ion and a rare gas atom can be described by a potential that is the sum of an unshielded Coulomb potential and an empirical polarization potential.

the angular distribution of the scattered ions exhibits a characteristic pattern of intensity maxima at scattering angles in order of 10 −4 < ϑ < 10 −3 rad, which cannot be explained by electron scattering theory, and which can be explained by an extended interaction potential, taking the charge distribution of the rare gas atom into account.

the study of the interaction of the Li7+-ion and the rare gas atoms.
the study of the interaction of Li7+ ions with atoms.
the study of the angular distribution of Li+ ions scattered by noble gas atoms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the angular distribution of the scattering intensity of Li+-ions on rare gas atoms is determined by the interaction potential of the charge distributions between the Li7+-ion and the rare gas atoms.

the angular distribution of Li+-ions scattered by the rare gases is due to the interaction of the charge distributions, and that the interaction potential between a Li+-ion and a rare gas atom is not a Coulomb potential, but a screened Coulomb potential with a polarization term.

the angular distribution of the scattered Li7+ ions at the scattering angles in the region of the intensity maxima cannot be interpreted by a simple potential scattering theory, but requires a theory of the interaction potential which takes into account the mutual action of charge distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the angular distribution of Li+-ions scattered by the rare gas atoms shows maxima at scattering angles in order of 10-4 rad.

the scattering of ions on rare gas atoms is a process which is not only governed by Coulomb forces, but also by the interaction between the charge distribution of the ion and that of the rare gas atom, i. e., the polarisation of the rare gas.
the scattering of Li7+- ions on rare gas atoms is not a pure Coulomb process, but that the polarisation of the rare gas atom plays an important part in the process of scattering.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a single, fixed value of the polarizability of a rare gas is not appropriate in the case of scattering of highly charged ions by rare gas atoms, because the polarizability is not a constant, but depends on the impact parameter.
the polarization of the rare gas atom by the Li7+-ion is the main reason for the existence of the intensity maxima.
the use of a single, fixed, and universal parameter for all the systems is not appropriate and should be avoided.
